title: Exploring the Synergy of Quantitative Factors and Newsflow Representations from Large Language Models for Stock Return Prediction

task.value: Predicting stock returns from multimodal quantitative factors and LLM-generated newsflow representations, used for stock selection into long-only and long-short portfolios.
task.quote: This paper examines effective methods for leveraging multimodal factors and newsflow in return prediction and stock selection.

architecture.value: News headlines encoded by an LLM into a newsflow vector; fused with ~200 factors via combination, summation or attention; a mixture model weights a factor-based dense network and a fusion component, trained with decoupled training (independent squared-error terms plus KL distribution matching).
architecture.quote: First, we introduce a fusion learning framework to learn a unified representation from factors and newsflow representations generated by an LLM. Within this framework, we compare three methods of different architectural complexities: representation combination, representation summation, and attentive representations.

data.value: North American, Emerging Markets and European universes (up to ~1,000 stocks each; 830/1090/370 stocks), ~200 quantitative factors, company-level news headlines from a commercial vendor; one-month forward return target, monthly rebalancing.
data.quote: We have three datasets corresponding to the North American (NA), Emerging Markets (EM), and European (EU) investment universes, each containing up to \sim 1,000 stocks. We use company-level financial news data provided by a commercial data vendor.

window.value: Training and validation 2003 to 2022; testing 2023 to 2024, evaluated without retraining.
window.quote: The training and validation data span from 2003 to 2022, and the testing data cover the two-year period from 2023 to 2024.

models.value: Encoder-only DeBERTa as the LLM for all methods, optionally fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 4) on all linear layers; dense neural networks for prediction components.
models.quote: For a fair comparison, we employ the encoder-only LLM, DeBERTa [31], across our fusion learning methods, mixture models, and all LLM-based baselines.

baselines.value: Equal-weighted Universe portfolio, Factors Alone dense network, News Alone (LLM representation plus prediction layer), and FININ; also compared across internal fusion variants and conventional-trained mixture.
baselines.quote: Universe refers to a portfolio that equally weights all stocks in the investment universe. Factors Alone represents a dense neural network solely on quantitative factors [17].

headline_result.value: NA universe, 2023-2024 test: Mixture Decoupled long-only 28.21% annual return (Sharpe 0.92), long-short 33.77% (Sharpe 1.78), IC 0.027; Fusion Combination long-only 32.43%; Factors Alone long-short 22.34%.

leakage_controls.value: Test period 2023-2024 chosen after DeBERTa's development (~2022) to mitigate LLM memorization bias; chose encoder-only DeBERTa over larger decoder LLMs that may memorize market information.
leakage_controls.quote: Since the LLM used in this paper, DeBERTa, was developed around 2022, we selected 2023-2024 as the testing period to mitigate potential memorization bias from the LLM [53, 42, 46].

limitations.value: News coverage is modest relative to all-cap universes; only headlines used, full article content left to future work; fine-tuning has inconsistent, universe-dependent impact; causes of weaker fusion methods need further investigation.
limitations.quote: Our investment universes include all-cap stocks, and the coverage of news data is modest relative to these universes. Consequently, there exist instances with only one news term, resulting in a low token count, sometimes fewer than 10, as shown in Table 5.
